newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand said to seek help on bills of exchange.
newsitem.headline: Thailand said to seek help on bills of exchange.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BOT) has asked foreign banks in Thailand to help draft regulations governing the issuance and trading of Bills of Exchange (B/E), the Foreign Banks' Assocation said on Monday.
"We had a meeting with them (BOT) last Thursday. And they asked us to do a study for them," Bruce Darrington, the chairman of Foreign Banks' Association, told Reuters.
"We want to work with the Bank of Thailand to assist them to regulate the market by using our expertise in international markets," he said.
B/E's are orders to pay a specified amount of money to holders either at a future date or on presentation of the bill.
In Thailand, B/E trading has grown substantially this year because of attractive yields and short maturities, analysts said.
But some recent interest and principal defaults by some B/E issuers had made foreigners more cautious and prompted all government agencies to clesely monitor B/E trading, they added.
